notes.text:
Trader Joe’s uses Service Channel and the Service Channel mobile app.
Customer Rules Must be followed! Note: Service Channel recognizes the phone GPS so tech needs to be within 2 miles of the store to log in/out.
 ***IMPORTANT*** If you are unable to log in or out of Service Channel – you can use our phone based automated response system (IVR) by dialing 516-500-7776. Take pictures of login error and save to dispatch
Techs need to check into Service Channel work order when arriving on location.
1.	After checking into Service Channel, techs should head in store and ask to speak with Captain/Manager on Duty. Introduce yourself and explain why you are onsite.
2.	Once you are shown equipment needing diagnosing, take pictures of data tags and asset tags. Specifically, pictures of Model and Serial number are mandatory.
3.	Once diagnosis is complete, confirm NTE on work order and determine if fixes can be completed same day.  
4.	If yes, assuming under NTE, tech can source parts locally to complete same day repairs but MUST call Climate Pros purchasing team for Tech PO (630-283-7316).
5.	If yes, but NTE will be exceeded, techs need to call their SM or CSS Keri Adams at 224-315-7139.
6.	If no verbal approval is given, techs need to move dispatch to PUR: NEED PARTS and check out of store with MOD.
7.	All return work MUST be quoted and submitted to the FM for approval unless verbal approval has been obtained.
8.	Once back in vehicle, techs should update FJX dispatch notes AND Service Channel work order notes. 
9.	Move Service Channel work order to correct status:
10.	In Progress/Incomplete or In Progress/Awaiting Quote if we cannot repair same day. 
11.	COMPLETED/PENDING CONFIRMATION if work is complete.

***Refrigerant adds - All refrigerant adds MUST be logged in SC and in dispatch notes. NO EXCEPTIONS. Dispatch notes, parts tab, and refrigerant tracking form should match the amount of the gas add.  Once refrigerant added, Service Channel work order should be moved to COMPLETED/PENDING REFRIGERANT USE so Customer Success Teams can track usage. Techs need to be mindful of question about refrigerant use in Service Channel. If refrigerant is used, they must answer YES.**

***Trader Joe’s EMS/Monitoring is R3 Contacts
Rick Furgison 971-235-4175
Cristian Alexander 509-496-9772
Travis Rider 702-592-5151

***ACORN RELATED ISSUES - If you are on a Trader Joe's Call and find that the issue is related to Acorn, please call 24hr #860-863-5924 for Power & Process***  

For any other questions about Trader Joe’s, please email Traderjoes@climatepros.com or call Keri Adams (Customer Success Supervisor) at (224) 315-7139

notes.text:
****MUST CHECK IF WE HAVE SURPLUS GAS CUSTOMER OWNED BEFORE PURCHASING GAS FOR ANY SAVE MART LOCATIONS****
If the work is out of contract, a quote is required and must go through the approval process.
   •   Save Mart is temporarily prioritizing only emergency and life safety-related repairs. Quotes that do not get approved will be placed on hold.
   •   If you need help determining whether a repair qualifies as an emergency or life safety issue, please reach out to your Service Manager.
****Anyone adding refrigerant over 50# to a Save Mart/Food Maxx/Lucky supermarket needs to be emailing savemart@climatepros.com and your service manager, with the dispatch number, amount of refrigerant that was added, type of gas, where was the leak and if it is repaired. The Save Mart Account Team needs the heads up to notify Save Mart. This needs to come from the technician in the field that is adding the refrigerant.****
****Checking in/out and pausing process for Save mart in the Corrigo app.****
SECOND TECH MUST LEAVE A NOTE WITH TIME AND DATE IN CORRIGO.
•	 When tech gets onsite, please check in Corrigo and manager.
•	If tech needs to place work order in follow up, needs parts etc... Tech is to place the work order on pause with a note. “Need to order parts” Or “Needs to quote repairs” as well as the visible to customer note tech would add to FJX.
•	Select ALL on the drop-down menu.
•	When tech is 100% complete with the work order we can then select the “check out” option. 
•	Once the tech selects “check out” a box will populate with “Work done description” and “Repair category”. In the work done description techs need to put in notes of the work done like they would do their FJX notes stating “call complete”
•	Final step is to fill out the fields asking to enter “Model number” “Serial number” and “LBS lost”

I had to fill the trash can with water about 7 times to fully de-ice the case. I was watching the temp drop, but due to the store closing, I didn't see it hit setpoint, but it was cooling and everything was working.

Store : Publix #1495. Refrigerant type: Glycol. Liquid level: 40%. Equipment: Deli walk-in cooler. Third party check in: PFS. Issue:  Cooler not maintaining set point. Resolution: I arrived and checked in with the MIC, arrived at the deli and checked in with the deli manager, fans were running but poor airflow and  the evaporator was spewing water out of the front. I went and retrieved a six foot ladder from the truck, returned and shut the fans off, a lot of water poured out of the evaporator, I opened the drain pan and found that there was a thick layer of mold and mildew buildup inside, which clogged the drain and the fans were pulling water up inside of the coil which restricted the airflow. I cleaned the drain pan out, blew the drain clear with  CO2, cleaned the bottom of the evaporator coil, added some drain treatment, tested the drain by flushing with water, I reinstalled the drain pan, the box now has good airflow and is pulling down in temperature. Moving to close this call.
Photos attached: Yes. No parts were needed. Job status: Complete. Third party check out: PFS.

Arrived on site and checked in with MOD to investigate Walk in cooler sliding door had fallen off the rails.

Located equipment and found door suspended by only 1 roller and had jumped off the guid rail. 

Was able to lift door and set back into place. Began inspecting the cause finding the lower right hand floor guide had became loose and was  installed in the wrong location. Made adjustment to door height and leveled out rolling assembly. Removed lower guide to find multiple holes drilled into the floor, old studs left prevent the guid from proper orientation, and the roller itself not making contact to keep the door pressed inward and not pop out.

No space was available to drill new anchors. Cleaned out original holes, fabricated a new, 1/2” longer mounting bracket, cut old studs out, and secured everything with new hardware. Lubricated all bearding and roller surfaces before testing door. 

Door now closes and maintains inward pressure to alleviate it sliding off the rails again.

Notified MOD of findings and corrective maintenance performed. Job completed.

Arrived on site for repairing Cooler 3 first evaporator and looking at Cooler 1 (Evap C) leaking water.

Checked in with store leadership and unloaded tools and equipment from the truck. Located the cooler and had product removed from underneath the evaporator. Was notified the store team could not provide a lift to access the evaporator at that time. Checked the facility for a scissor lift and found none available.

Gained access to the area underneath the evaporator and cleared the drain line with nitrogen. Filled a bucket with water, set up a submersible pump, and ran extension cords and hoses to begin deicing the evaporator. Due to the thickness of the ice, multiple trips were required to refill the bucket. Airflow has been restored, further ice accumulation has been prevented, and the drain is now flowing properly.

Part 2/2

Then began working on Evaporator C in Cooler 1. Found excessive water spraying from the evaporator. Gained access underneath the evaporator and inspected the drain system. Found the drain line clear; however, water was not flowing into the drain pan properly. Checked the drain pan level and found it was not pitched correctly toward the drain. Adjusted the drain pan assembly to restore proper pitch, but water still would not flow toward the drain.

Observed the water being affected by the airflow from the fans. Checked airflow through the evaporator and found very little air moving through the coil, with airflow instead blowing into the drain pan area.

At this time the store team was able to assist with setting up a lift. Checked airflow directly in front of the fans and found air pushing out the sides instead of straight ahead. De-energized the fans and inspected blade depth and orientation. The only issue found was a plastic bag tangled in one of the fan blades, which was removed.

Filled a bucket and raised it up with the lift to reduce the pressure drop from the height. Applied food-safe coil cleaner and sprayed the coil from behind. Retested airflow and found the water  was still being affected and poor airflow.

Retrieved a more powerful submersible pump because of the thickness of the coil.  Attempted to flush the coil from both the front and rear to completely clear any debris. Found no improvement in airflow. This indicates the coil is deeply impacted with debris, restricting proper airflow and drainage, and will require cleaning with an electric power washer while using a lift.

Notified GM Ray of the findings. He advised shutting off Evaporator C in Cooler 1 until repairs can be completed to prevent further water from spraying onto product.

Cleaned up work area and notified store leadership.
No injuries were reported on this job.

A note on HVAC units:

H-E-B will not pay for any refrigerant add that is not documented within the 72 hour window.

This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.

Instead, technicians and/or vendor recordkeepers MUST create a “call log” in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add, documenting: 
•	The appliance serviced.
•	The refrigerant type added.
•	Total amount of refrigerant recovered (if any)
•	Total amount of refrigerant added (including adding back recovered refrigerant)
•	Date refrigerant was added. 
•	Leak location(s) 

There will be an additional optional free text space for other notes.  

**PLEASE copy and paste the following link to access the HEB COMPRESSOR REPLACEMENT FORM:

https://url.us.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/OVkRCQWRVRFxmxD1SxfnTGgCW1?domain=app.smartsheet.com

Technicians and/or vendor record keepers MUST record refrigerant adds on the following appliance types:
•	Any refrigeration appliance except for self-contains (e.g., bottle coolers on the store floor), regardless of charge size.
•	Any HVAC appliance, regardless of charge size
A note on HVAC units:
If refrigerant is required for an HVAC unit with multiple independent circuits/stages, keep in mind that each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance, so refrigerant adds on each circuit must be logged individually.
?	Example: if tech is working on PACU2, an HVAC unit with 4 separate circuits/stages, and wants to add gas to circuit 1 (PACU2a) and circuit 3 (PACU2c), tech or recordkeeper must enter a separate call log for PACU2a and PACU2c with the amount of refrigerant added.

Call logs are required to be entered in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add. Failing to create a call log to record the refrigerant add within 72 hours is the equivalent of not getting approval to add the refrigerant. H-E-B will not pay for any refrigerant add that is not documented within the 72 hour window.

This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.

H-E-B’S REFRIGERANT MANAGEMENT PROTOCOLS HAVE NOT CHANGED!

Instead, technicians and/or vendor recordkeepers MUST create a “call log” in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add, documenting:

Technicians and/or vendor record keepers MUST record refrigerant adds on the following appliance types:
•	Any refrigeration appliance except for self-contains (e.g., bottle coolers on the store floor), regardless of charge size.
•	Any HVAC appliance, regardless of charge size
A note on HVAC units:
If refrigerant is required for an HVAC unit with multiple independent circuits/stages, keep in mind that each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance, so refrigerant adds on each circuit must be logged individually.
?	Example: if tech is working on PACU2, an HVAC unit with 4 separate circuits/stages, and wants to add gas to circuit 1 (PACU2a) and circuit 3 (PACU2c), tech or recordkeeper must enter a separate call log for PACU2a and PACU2c with the amount of refrigerant added.

Call logs are required to be entered in MyFacility within 72 hours of the refrigerant add. Failing to create a call log to record the refrigerant add within 72 hours is the equivalent of not getting approval to add the refrigerant. H-E-B will not pay for any refrigerant add that is not documented within the 72 hour window.

This requirement applies to ANY store/facility, any refrigerant type, including CO2, and any type of leak repair, including warranty work or any other special project.
